newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were expected to open slightly lower Wednesday after a further build in LME and COMEX warehouse copper stocks.
COMEX September copper was called unchanged to down 0.30 cent from Tuesday's close of 107.20 cents a lb after trading from 107.40 to 106.45 cents on ACCESS.
LME copper stocks rose a further 4,300 tonnes Wednesday to 244,975 tonnes, the highest levels in nearly a year, while COMEX copper stocks were up 1,595 short tons Tuesday at 31,970 short tons.
Copper prices have been struggling to recover from a three-month low posted in mid-July after the rise in exchange stocks brought a 12-month-long rally to an end.

In other news, a strike at Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury complex in Canada entered its sixth day, but the company's Timmins refinery in Ontario continues to operate, there are hopes talks between union and management will resume this week.
The mine produced 50,000 tonnes of copper last year, 2 percent of North American production or 0.6 percent of Western World production.
